title: Many Travelers Become Different People on Vacation
paragraphs: Do you behave differently when you are on vacation? If so, you are certainly not alone. According to recent surveys, a large number of travelers say they become noticeably different people when they are away from home.

In one survey, the results of which were reported in September 2026, Hint, an app that offers advice based on astrology, questioned 14,673 adults in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, the European Union, Australia and Latin America. It found that 61% of respondents deliberately behave differently while traveling, even though many of them described themselves as predictable or routine-driven in their everyday lives.

Moreover, 47% said they had knowingly done something on a trip because it felt appropriate at the time, even though they would probably have rejected the same idea at home. In addition, 42% said they had stayed out later than they wanted so that they would not "waste" an evening of their holiday, and 38% had bought something they would normally consider unnecessary because it was connected to their memories of the trip. Perhaps unsurprisingly, 35% said they had returned home surprised by something they had done or agreed to while they were away.

Other research has found similar results. For example, in a survey of more than 28,000 travelers by the travel company Booking.com, 77% said they were interested in taking a holiday specifically to do something completely out of character.

Why does this happen? According to one explanation, travelers feel more free to stay out late, spend money or say yes to things they would usually refuse. Purchases may seem easier to justify when they are linked to a place a person may never visit again, while an evening out may feel more valuable because the number of holiday evenings is limited.

However, it is not clear whether people show their "true selves" on vacation. Instead, the results may simply suggest that people's everyday routines are more flexible than they think. It should also be noted that both surveys were carried out by companies rather than independent researchers.
